treaty_name: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Republic of Kenya for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (2016; modified by MLI)
eif_quote: Art. 31(2): 'This Agreement shall enter into force on the date of the later of the notifications referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article.' Entry-into-force date 2017-08-30 taken from map.json (India MLI position); Kenya Legal Notice No. 147 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 115, 28th July, 2017) declares the arrangements 'signed on the 11th July, 2016'.
source_title: Kenya Legal Notice No. 147 of 2017 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 115), Schedule: Kenya-India DTA 2016 (Wayback copy of the Kenya Law official PDF, captured 2021-11-11)

rates.quote: 2. However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

2. However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

2. However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 percent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: 1. Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement.

notes: Effective (Art. 31(3)): Kenya, taxes withheld at source on amounts paid or credited on or after 1 January 2018; India, fiscal years beginning on or after 1 April 2018. Replaced the 1985 India-Kenya agreement (15%/15%/20%). Not modelled: Art. 11(3) exemption for interest beneficially owned by Governments, political sub-divisions, local authorities, RBI, Exim Bank of India, Central Bank of Kenya or agreed institutions; fees for management, professional and technical services are a separate Art. 13 (not a royalty). Treaty Art. 29 'Limitation of Benefits' already contains a main-purpose test (Art. 29(2)) and bona-fide business requirement (Art. 29(3)). Indian notification for this treaty reported as No. 11/2018 (not read - egazette/incometaxindia not reachable). MLI: covered by both; MLI WHT provisions effective 2026-01-01 on the Kenyan side (Kenya MLI in force 2025-05-01); India chose Art. 35(2) 'taxable period', so on the Indian side from 1 April 2026. Both India and Kenya chose the Simplified LOB (Art. 7(6)), so the SLOB applies in addition to the PPT.
unverified: Entry-into-force date from map.json; Indian Notification 11/2018 not read
Indian-side MLI date 2026-04-01 derived from India's Art. 35(2) choice
